staged_original_note: The twice-rebuilt file, UNCHANGED at Book XII step 1. It was rebuilt at Book IV step 1 (three PG illustration captions; 7bf2d1b1... -> b0ecf3da...) and at Book VII step 1 (three of Long's footnotes printed flush left; b0ecf3da... -> 7798607d...). For Book XII the check was NOT a re-run of the build script; the reconstruction's own RULES were audited against the raw range before its output was looked at; and the reconstruction derives the chapter by a rule of a DIFFERENT KIND from the build's, which is the standard the Book XI reviewer set. The build keys on an [A-D] opener and then consumes every following indented OR BLANK line until flush-left text resumes. scripts/verify_book12_source.py, written from scratch, instead splits the range into blank-line-separated blocks and classifies each by its INDENTATION PROFILE, with no opener state and no consumption: first line flush left = body; every line indented four or more = apparatus; every line indented but minimum indentation below four = verse, joined into the body paragraph before it. RESULT: 36 reconstructed paragraphs, matching the staged count, and THE ONLY DIFFERENCE IN THE WHOLE BOOK IS THE SINGLE DAGGER MARK at XII.16 (PG 6963), which PROVENANCE.md section 4 documents as deliberately removed. The dagger was deliberately left IN the reconstruction so that it would surface as a diff and be counted; the paragraph differs by that one '+' and by nothing else. Rule audit, class by class over PG 6818-7174 (after the XII. header at 6817, before INDEXES. at 7175): FOURTEEN maximal indented runs enumerated with their indentation profiles -- eleven footnote openers, all indented four spaces (PG 6883, 6888, 6969, 6974, 7017, 7052, 7069, 7079, 7123, 7168, 7170); two unmarked continuations of a footnote body, each checked BY CONTENT to follow the run it belongs to with only blank lines between (PG 6886, and PG 7092-7102, the second half of the long note opened at 7079); and one verse run, Long's line of Empedocles at PG 6866, indented THREE spaces. A FINDING ABOUT METHOD, NOT ABOUT THE TEXT: PG 6886 is indented NINE spaces, so the Book XI reviewer's own alternative rule ('drop the four-space runs') would have kept it and leaked [Greek: Sphairos kykloteres monie perigethei gaion.] into the body of XII.4 (CORRECTED from 'XII.3' at acceptance, round-1 finding C1: the reviewer implemented the alternative rule and ran it, and the block at PG 6886 stands between the end of XII.4 at PG 6881 and the start of XII.5 at PG 6890). A number taken from one book does not transfer to the next; the SHAPE of the rule does. ELEVEN in-text markers -- ten in flush-left text (PG 6879, 6964, 6967, 7008, 7046, 7062, 7073, 7111, 7155, 7160) plus one at the end of the indented verse line 6866 -- RECONCILING EXACTLY with the eleven openers. NO flush-left footnote opener (the VII.45 class). NO illustration caption (the Book IV class). Twenty-four short standalone flush-left lines, every one the wrapped tail of a paragraph ending in terminal punctuation, so no running head, page number or catchword. NO Greek in the body: all four [Greek: ...] spans in the range (PG 6886, 6969, 6971, 7069) are inside indented footnote bodies, and the staged Book XII contains no '(Greek:' at all. Underscores only inside footnote bodies (7087, 7089, 7094). D14 checked: the space-before-punctuation rule does not fire anywhere in this range, and is reproduced in the reconstruction regardless so that the two are compared on the same rules. sha256 unchanged at 7798607d..., 487 paragraphs, twelve chapters, section profile 17, 17, 16, 51, 36, 59, 75, 61, 42, 38, 39, 36, git status clean, so NO REBUILD was made and no accepted book is reopened.

dagger_marks: ONE, at XII.16 (PG line 6963), matching PROVENANCE.md section 4. Long uses the dagger for a place where the Greek is corrupt. The clause stands as Long has it, with the pronoun modernised and HIS COMMA KEPT, on the X.25 ruling: 'If then you are irritable, cure this man's disposition.' Nothing in it is made clearer than the source. Book XII has fewer dagger marks than any other book in the work.

shall_rule: Long has 10 'shall / shalt' in Book XII. The accepted candidate keeps NONE. Nine were removed at v1, every one a plain future (XII.1 x4, XII.3 x2, XII.4 third person, XII.15 a rhetorical future in a direct question, XII.36 a noun clause). The tenth, XII.4's first-person 'what we shall think of ourselves', was kept at v1 under the rule's first-person licence and is converted at v2 on round-1 finding 4.1: the licence is that the 'shall' be current English IN ITS OWN RIGHT, and in a two-member comparison whose other member has just taken 'will' it reads as marking a difference the sentence denies. The rule's other instances (II.1, VIII.45, X.6 x5, XI.18 x2) are all unpaired and are untouched. LONG'S 'WILT', decided once at v2 (finding 1.1 with 3.2): the rule governs 'shall / shalt' only, and v1 dropped 'wilt' at XII.1 and kept it as 'will' at XII.3 twice; v2 aligns all three on the plain present, which is what English uses in an if-clause. Book XII adds no new case to the three third-person plain futures standing in accepted books (III.9, VII.8, VII.24) -- and the cross-book pass re-derives that class, which is larger than three.
base_text_defects: XII.27, a PG slip, FLAGGED and CORRECTED: PG 'Stertinius at Briae', SE 'Baiae'. Rendered 'Baiae'. Briae is not a place; Baiae is the Roman seaside resort, and it stands in a list of retreats beside 'Tiberius at Capreae'. One of TWO departures from PG's letters in Book XII.

XII.29, a PG slip, FLAGGED and CORRECTED: PG 'what it is itself, THAT is its material', SE 'WHAT is its material'. Rendered 'what is its matter'. PG's reading makes a thing's matter be what the thing 'is itself', which is the distinction the meditation exists to draw, and breaks a three-member series whose third member has already elided its verb. The second of the two departures.
XII.5, PG right and SE wrong: PG 'disputing with the Deity', SE 'diety', which is not a word. PG followed.
XII.14, PG right and SE wrong: PG 'a confusion without A governor'; SE drops the article. PG followed.
XII.24, PG right and SE wrong: PG 'beings who dwell ALL around in the air'; SE drops 'all'. PG followed.
XII.27, an open variant: PG 'Fabius Catellinus', SE 'Catullinus'. Both are possible Roman cognomina and nothing in the sentence decides. PG followed under D6 and the X.27 ruling on Latin name forms.
XII.23, an open variant: PG 'moved towards the same THING in his mind', SE 'the same THINGS'. PG followed under D6.
XII.1, a spelling variant that does not reach the candidate: PG 'thou mayst', SE 'mayest'. Both become 'you may' under the thou-rule. The X.32 / XI.15 case in this book's form.

XII.12, a PG typographic slip INSIDE apparatus: the cross-reference reads '(ii. 11, 12, 13; vii. 62; 18 viii. 17)', a stray numeral with no referent. The span is dropped as apparatus, so the slip never reaches the candidate.

XII.2 / XII.6 / XII.16, typographic: PG 'such like' (SE 'suchlike') rendered 'of that kind' on the XI.1 ruling; both texts print 'fig-tree', normalised to 'fig tree' under X.36.2; PG 'Practise / practised' at XII.6 normalised to the American 'practice / practiced', which PG itself uses elsewhere.
Standard Ebooks prints Book XII with page numbers in the text flow and omits every cross-reference. Neither is a reading; the paragraph count is 36 in both.
cross_book_inconsistencies_noticed_not_r: 'Such like': the accepted Book IX keeps it at IX.1, while Book XI rendered it 'things of that kind' at XI.1 and Book XII follows XI at XII.2. IX.1's acceptance is closed; the divergence is formal, not semantic. Recorded in 00-progress-ledger.md under 'Open, not blocking'.
The plural distributive 'several': the accepted Book V keeps it at V.1, while Book XI rendered it 'separate' at XI.2 and Book XII follows XI at XII.30. Same class, same disposition.

'Adapted to' in the dead sense of 'suited to': round-1 finding 34.1 retires it at XII.34, and the round-1 reviewer's frequency table finds it standing at V.8, VI.16 and X.11 in accepted books. Not reopened book by book; carried to the cross-book pass, where the decision is taken once.
rulings_round_1: XII.27 'Baiae' and XII.29 'what': BOTH CONFIRMED, each on its own evidence; XII.29 is the stronger of the two. The number of departures in a book is a symptom, not a standard.

XII.3's '[to the god that is within thee]' under D11: CONFIRMED, route and outcome. The VII.17 alternative declined -- VII.13/VII.17 keep Long's Greek because those meditations ARE arguments about the Greek words, and XII.3 contains no such argument.

XII.17's '[For let thy efforts be-]' as a mark of textual doubt: CONFIRMED, and D13's Book XI amendment ('voice and subject, not length') supports extending the class from a word to a clause. D13's sentence is widened at acceptance to 'a word or a clause', naming XI.26 and XII.17 (C3).
XII.4's 'shall' beside 'will': RULED FOR 'WILL' IN BOTH (finding 4.1); applied at v2.
XII.27's '[or Rufus at Velia]' under D11: CONFIRMED. D11 reaches an alternative CONSTRUAL; unlike the XI.26/XII.17 class the words cannot stand as text once the mark is removed.

XII.23's two resumptive repairs: ALLOWED, with finding 23.1 correcting their stated ground (the resumptive 'he' IS dropped in each, two words in all; v1's 'no word is added or dropped' was false and is withdrawn).
The added commas: four of the five earned, XII.15's second not (15.1), and there are six, not five (2.1).
D13 fires nowhere in Book XII: AGREED, tested bracket by bracket. X.23 remains its only instance in the work.
The XII.12 stray '18' never reaches the candidate: CONFIRMED.

The step-1 no-rebuild finding: UPHELD by a THIRD reconstruction of a THIRD kind (review/verify_book12_source_review.py, which uses no indentation magnitude at all and decides each indented run by sentence continuity in the body accumulated so far): 36 paragraphs, one differing paragraph, XII.16, differing only by the documented dagger.
